 LocalAI runs open models for chat, images, speech and video on your own machines. The API speaks the OpenAI and Anthropic formats. Your team gets chats, files and documents on top, and the assistant can write and run code. It runs on a laptop, a server, in a container or on Kubernetes, and a distributed mode spreads models over several machines. No GPU needed, though a GPU makes it faster.

- Chats, agents, Projects and a team : chats and saved agents that use tools, MCP servers, files, Knowledge collections and skills. Projects group chats, files, notes and agents around one piece of work. Users, roles, quotas and shared folders for a team (development builds).
- Add-ons : an admin installs add-ons from a library: Office, Sandbox, Tables, chat apps, mail, calendar and more.
- Every kind of model, one API : text, vision, speech to text, text to speech, images, video, music and sound, embeddings and reranking, in the OpenAI and Anthropic formats (with ElevenLabs-compatible text to speech and sound generation), with more than 80 backends. Each backend is its own image, pulled only when a model needs it.
- Your hardware : NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Apple Silicon, Vulkan, NVIDIA Jetson or CPU only. The server, the models and your files stay on your own machines.

 

Created by Ettore Di Giacinto and maintained by the LocalAI team.

 Quick start

 Script (Linux, and macOS on Apple Silicon): it downloads the release binary for your machine and checks it against the release checksums.

 

The script installs the program and does not start it; local-ai starts the server. To run a model directly, name it, for example local-ai run gemma-4-e2b-it-qat-q4 0 , a small Google Gemma 4 model for CPUs (4.3 GB to download: 3.35 GB for the model and 0.99 GB for the image projector).

 Container (Docker, podman, ...):

 

 Desktop app : it installs, updates, starts and stops the server for you and shows the web interface in its own window, on macOS and Linux. It is in the 5.0 release. Download it from the latest release. See the desktop app guide.

The install script and the latest image give 5.0.0.

Then open To restart an existing container, use docker start -i local-ai . More ways to install: Install LocalAI.

 
 GPU images (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Vulkan) 

 

LocalAI detects your GPU and downloads the matching backend. See GPU Acceleration.

 

Load a model:

 

To talk to a running server from the terminal, start the built-in agent in another shell. It asks you to approve anything that changes state. See the Terminal agent docs.

 

More in the Quickstart.

 What you can do

 Area What it gives you 
 --- --- 
 Chats Conversations the server keeps, with saved agents that use tools, MCP, skills and files, triggers, and chat apps 
 Add-ons Office, Sandbox, Tables, chat apps, mail, calendar and more install from a library and run beside the server 
 Text generation llama.cpp , transformers , vllm ... and more, with an OpenAI-compatible tools API and constrained grammars 
 Music and sound Make music and sound effects from a text prompt with /v1/sound-generation . See text to audio 
 Speech Text to audio, audio to text, voice activity detection (Silero-VAD) and the Realtime API for speech-to-speech 
 Images, video and vision Image generation, video generation, the Vision API and object detection 
 Search Embeddings and a reranker 
 Operations API key auth, user quotas and roles, distributed mode (PostgreSQL + NATS) and P2P inferencing 
 Models and backends Models from Hugging Face and a Backend Gallery to install or remove backends on the fly, plus the integrated web UI 

LocalAI has more than 80 backends. Hardware acceleration covers NVIDIA (CUDA 12 and 13), AMD (ROCm), Intel (oneAPI/SYCL), Apple Silicon (Metal), Vulkan and NVIDIA Jetson (L4T). See the Backend and Model Compatibility Table.

 Backends we build

Most backends wrap an upstream engine such as llama.cpp or vLLM. We wrote 18 of them ourselves: native C, C++ and GGML engines with no Python at inference.

 Backend What it does 
 --------- ------------- 
 vllm.cpp From-scratch C++20 port of vLLM for text generation: paged KV cache, continuous batching, prefix caching, safetensors + GGUF loading, engine-enforced structured output, on CPU, CUDA, Metal and Vulkan. Also serves MiniMax-H3 joint video+audio generation 
 parakeet.cpp C++/GGML port of NVIDIA NeMo Parakeet ASR (tdt/ctc/rnnt/hybrid), with cache-aware streaming transcription 
 moss-transcribe.cpp C++/GGML port of OpenMOSS MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize: joint long-form transcription, speaker diarization and timestamping in a single pass 
 moss-tts.cpp C++/GGML port of the OpenMOSS MOSS-TTS family: text-to-speech (MOSS-TTS-Local v1.5, 48 kHz stereo) with reference-audio voice cloning, through the MOSS-Audio-Tokenizer neural codec 
 magpie-tts.cpp C++/GGML port of NVIDIA's Magpie TTS Multilingual 357M: 22.05 kHz mono text-to-speech in 5 voices and 9+ languages, with the NanoCodec neural codec and tokenizer/G2P embedded in a single GGUF 
 ced.cpp C++/GGML port of the CED audio-tagging models: sound-event classification (527-class AudioSet) over REST and the realtime API for live recognition 
 voice-detect.cpp Speaker recognition and voice analysis (ECAPA-TDNN, WeSpeaker, ERes2Net, CAM++, wav2vec2 age/gender/emotion), replacing the Python speaker-recognition backend 
 vibevoice.cpp Native port of Microsoft VibeVoice for TTS (voice cloning) and long-form ASR with speaker diarization 
 rf-detr.cpp Native RF-DETR object detection and instance segmentation 
 locate-anything.cpp Open-vocabulary object detection and visual grounding (LocateAnything-3B) 
 depth-anything.cpp Depth Anything 3 monocular metric depth + camera pose estimation 
 face-detect.cpp Face detection, recognition, demographics and anti-spoofing (SCRFD/ArcFace, YuNet/SFace), replacing the Python insightface backend 
 timestral.cpp Mistral Timestral time-series forecasting: quantile forecasts with

install.title: Quick start
install.html:
Script (Linux, and macOS on Apple Silicon): it downloads the release binary for your machine and checks it against the release checksums.

curl -sSL https://localai.io/install.sh | sh
local-ai
# open http://localhost:8080 and install a model from there

The script installs the program and does not start it; local-ai starts the server. To run a model directly, name it, for example local-ai run gemma-4-e2b-it-qat-q4_0, a small Google Gemma 4 model for CPUs (4.3 GB to download: 3.35 GB for the model and 0.99 GB for the image projector).

Container (Docker, podman, ...):

docker run -ti --name local-ai -p 8080:8080 localai/localai:latest

Desktop app: it installs, updates, starts and stops the server for you and shows the web interface in its own window, on macOS and Linux. It is in the 5.0 release. Download it from the latest release. See the desktop app guide.

The install script and the latest image give 5.0.0.

Then open http://localhost:8080. To restart an existing container, use docker start -i local-ai. More ways to install: Install LocalAI.

GPU images (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Vulkan)
# NVIDIA, CUDA 13
docker run -ti --name local-ai -p 8080:8080 --gpus all localai/localai:latest-gpu-nvidia-cuda-13

# NVIDIA, CUDA 12
docker run -ti --name local-ai -p 8080:8080 --gpus all localai/localai:latest-gpu-nvidia-cuda-12

# NVIDIA Jetson ARM64 (CUDA 12, for AGX Orin and similar)
docker run -ti --name local-ai -p 8080:8080 --gpus all localai/localai:latest-nvidia-l4t-arm64

# NVIDIA Jetson ARM64 (CUDA 13, for DGX Spark)
docker run -ti --name local-ai -p 8080:8080 --gpus all localai/localai:latest-nvidia-l4t-arm64-cuda-13

# AMD (ROCm)
docker run -ti --name local-ai -p 8080:8080 --device=/dev/kfd --device=/dev/dri --group-add=video localai/localai:latest-gpu-hipblas

# Intel (oneAPI)
docker run -ti --name local-ai -p 8080:8080 --device=/dev/dri/card1 --device=/dev/dri/renderD128 localai/localai:latest-gpu-intel

# Vulkan
docker run -ti --name local-ai -p 8080:8080 localai/localai:latest-gpu-vulkan

LocalAI detects your GPU and downloads the matching backend. See GPU Acceleration.

Load a model:

# From the model gallery (list it with `local-ai models list` or on the Models page of the web UI)
local-ai run gemma-4-e2b-it-qat-q4_0
# From Hugging Face
local-ai run huggingface://TheBloke/phi-2-GGUF/phi-2.Q8_0.gguf
# From the Ollama OCI registry
local-ai run ollama://gemma:2b
# From a standard OCI registry (for example Docker Hub)
local-ai run oci://localai/phi-2:latest

To talk to a running server from the terminal, start the built-in agent in another shell. It asks you to approve anything that changes state. See the Terminal agent docs.

local-ai chat --model gemma-4-e2b-it-qat-q4_0

More in the Quickstart.
